paragraphs: (“And the sons of Sheshan: Achlai,” [I Chronicles 2:31](https://www.sefaria.org/I_Chronicles.2.31).) He is mentioned in [Eruvin 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12a.7): “Rav Achlai said — and some say Rav Yechiel”; Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Ahlai.

Yuchasin wrote that he lived in Shmuel’s time, deriving this from the fact that there an objection is raised from Rav Achlai to what Shmuel said to Rabbi Chananyah bar Shila. Hyman objects that this is no proof at all, for it is known…

notes.text: The supplied text breaks off here. The [later discussion on 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.12a.20-23) compares the Achlai or Yechiel ruling with Shmuel’s. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=379&lang=en) places Achlai in Shmuel’s time, as Hyman says Yuchasin does. Hyman disputes that inference.

Hyman’s printed entry continues over the page break (vol. I, pp. 137–138). The omitted continuation says that Rav Yechiel lived much later than Shmuel and that Rav Pappa even raises an objection from Shmuel’s ruling against Rav Yechiel. It is Hyman’s argument about chronology. In the consulted Eruvin 12a, Rav Pappa introduces Shmuel’s ruling to Rav Chananya bar Sheila, and the discussion compares it with a ruling attributed alternatively to Rav Achlai or Rav Yechiel. One response distinguishes a courtyard from an alleyway. Hyman’s readings of Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim are reported from his entry.
